gaps.claim: The acceptance test cannot reach a remote escrow by construction; a proof replica is materialised locally first.
MODE_UNSUPPORTED has exactly one trigger; buildability of notProvidedPaths is left to the build.
The binary replica's contents are faithful to the named tier; its reachability is still simulated and the replay audit only measures file:// stores.
One added fixed-output source raised OBJECTS_REALISED by two, not the one predicted in DESIGN.md §20. Why is not established.
gaps.closeNote: Arithmetic, not a mystery, and the answer was three lines below the number in the same report. OBJECTS_REALISED is `nix-store --query --requisites --include-outputs` of the top derivation, and that set contains the .drv files themselves -- t15.13 says so in as many words. One added fixed-output source therefore adds TWO store objects: its .drv (text-CA) and its output (fixed-CA). The same report shows derivations 638->639 and ESCROW_OBJECTS_CONTENT_ADDRESSED 820->822, both consistent with +2 and both printed beside the number that was called unexplained. The pre-registration predicted +1 because it forgot a derivation is itself a store object, and it predicted the derivation count in the same table without joining the two rows.

gaps.claim: The binary-tier signature policy is exercised only against a local file:// tier signed by a locally generated key. No credential crosses a network and no real authenticated backend (S3, Attic, an HTTPS cache behind auth) has been tested, so what a real tier does with an expired or wrong credential is not established.

With a tier verified to hold an object carrying no signature at all, preserve materialised it and wrote a manifest: the SIGNATURE_UNTRUSTED branch did not fire (run 32, t24.11). Whether the cause is that this tool performs no signature check on the tier path, or that Nix does not verify signatures when the destination is a binary cache rather than a local store, is NOT established. t24.9/t24.10 measure it; no fix is being applied to preserve.sh until they answer.
